analysis:
ClusterPairTelemetry.swift (head lines 65-71, 77-78, 93, 197-198): adds optional `serving` (ClusterServedScope) and `tensorAssistant` (Bool) to the per-request telemetry record and to the served-speed bucket key. The fields carry values only, with no prompt text, token IDs or client identity, so A-001 exposure is unchanged. Both are optional with nil defaults, so older owner-only files still decode. The readers still use O_NOFOLLOW, an S_IFREG check and a 1 MiB cap, and writes still go through ClusterIncidentLog.writeAtomically. I found no new trust boundary. The type definition of ClusterServedScope is outside the supplied evidence.

Gemma4TensorParallelPagedSession.swift (head lines 166-199, 266-276): `decode` now shares a `decodeRow` helper with a new `submitDecode`. `submitDecode` takes the previous step's lazy agreed-token MLXArray, so the token is not host-validated against the vocabulary range the way `decode` validates it at line 150. The token comes from the rank's own choice/argmax graph, not from an external actor, so I treat this as a correctness-hardening note rather than a finding. The page guard (line 175: `pagesCover || reservePages`) matches `decode`'s. `reservePages` returns true when `pageGrowthTarget` is nil, so a one-ahead step at the request's final index could write past the reserved or maximum tokens. The doc says a step built after the request ended is evaluated and never committed. Whether `state.submit` and the request loop prevent a KV overflow or a leftover uncommitted step is not visible here. `withLayerStride` and `benchLayerStrideApplies` are public bench-only knobs and do not touch the wire.

Gemma4TensorParallelRequestLoop.swift: only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied (one-ahead step building, sampled and greedy paths, per-step logprobs). The body is not reviewed. Open questions for integration: (1) does the loop bound the speculative extra step, and does it ensure both ranks issue identical collectives so a stop or cancel cannot deadlock the pair (T-010, A-018 availability)? (2) are lazily held sampled-step logprobs and history bounded? (3) does `CBv2OwnedRequestState.submit` enforce the same token-count and page invariants as `run`?
